children: Indian equity markets are expected to open on a steady note on Tuesday amid positive global cues and a fall in crude oil prices. Gift Nifty at 23,510 indicates a small gain at open. According to analysts, the market will remain anchored by foreign news flows, especially from the US, Iran and the tariff front.

“Asian markets are taking positive cues from the overnight rally on Wall Street and the decline in crude oil prices. South Korea’s KOSPI is trading more than 2% higher, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 remains closed for a market holiday. GIFT Nifty futures are trading above 23,500 in early trade, compared with the Nifty 50’s previous close of 23,414, pointing to a firm opening for domestic equities. However, elevated geopolitical tensions are likely to keep investor sentiment guarded, with buying interest potentially remaining selective at higher levels,” said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money
WTI crude is trading in the $92–$93-a-barrel range, offering some relief on the broader macroeconomic front.

Macro indicators show improvement, but recovery remains uneven
Analysts also said macro numbers look better.

According to DSP Mutual Fund, the double-digit YoY growth in several demand indicators continues to be aided by a favourable base. “On an absolute basis, consumption indicators have improved, but the pickup remains uneven across segments.

Manufacturing continues to fare reasonably well. Credit growth, capital goods production and infrastructure activity remain considerably stronger than they were a year ago,” said but added caution, “However, manufacturing PMI has softened recently while WPI remains elevated.”

When valuations for India equities were sky high, we highlighted how fragile the system had become to foreign investment outflows. Today we are at the other end. At such valuations, the environment becomes particularly conducive to flows. But MF equity flows, which remained rather strong through most of the bull market, have begun to look patchy now, according to DSP Mutual.
Softer US yields offer some global relief

Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury yields have also eased, with the 10-year yield moving back below 5% after recently reaching multi-year highs. “The decline in yields, alongside softer oil prices, is helping improve the global risk backdrop. However, continued foreign selling remains a key headwind for Indian equities, even as sustained buying by domestic institutional investors provides some support,” said Ponmudi
Signal from derivative trading also turned positive, analysts said.

According to Dhupesh Dhameja, Derivatives Research Analyst, SAMCO Securities, the Derivatives setup has turned more supportive. PCR stands at 1.36, with total Put OI at 22.25 crore contracts versus Call OI of 15.15 crore. Strong Put concentration around 23,300–23,400 provides a firm near-term cushion, while Call OI is building across 23,500–24,000, creating layered resistance. “This positioning suggests that downside risk is currently better protected, but the upside may remain capped until Call-side supply starts shifting higher,” he said.
India VIX declined 1.43% to 11.22, indicating subdued volatility and supporting a gradual recovery environment.

“Overall, the bias is cautiously constructive above 23,270. Sustained buying above 23,500 can trigger further short covering towards 23,590–23,667, whereas failure to hold 23,270 would weaken the recovery and bring 23,060 back into focus,” he added.

title: Sensex, Nifty set for steady opening amid positive global cues
